q-177650.name: Question 1
q-177650.problem: Let $I=[0,1]⊂R$ and ${X}_{i}=[0,i]\times \{i\}.$ Which of the following represents ${⋃}_{i\in I}{X}_{i}?$
q-177650.worked_solution:
Recall that the union of a family of indexed sets consists of those elements that belong to *at least one* set:

$$
{⋃}_{i\in I}{A}_{i}=\{x\,:\,x\in {A}_{k}\,\,\text{for at least one}\,\,k\in I\}
$$

Let's now write down one of our indexed sets. For example, if $i=0.5,$ we have 

$$
{X}_{0.5}=[0,0.5]\times \{0.5\}=\{(k,0.5)\,:\,k\in [0,0.5]\}.
$$

This represents a horizontal line segment from the point $(0,0.5)$ to the point $(0.5,0.5)$ in the coordinate plane, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14167512/assets/7587daeaea45c5ef3449ecb676133c60bbedb7819308783bac835f3ae9c6883c.png)

In general,

$$
{X}_{i}=[0,i]\times \{i\}=\{(k,i)\,:\,k\in [0,i]\}
$$

is the horizontal line segment from the point $(0,i)$ to the point $(i,i).$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14167512/assets/b926204a3d58b25889f1c79dd0f65c1ea990c67bc88e869004396a77970e8dd4.png)

As $i$ runs over $I,$ these line segments sweep the following triangle that represents the union ${⋃}_{i\in I}{X}_{i}:$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14167512/assets/4a81de1a698eedf6a636d66b68a7c62efa69d1d026a961ae97ab5ecc2ef9828d.png)

q-181306.name: Question 2
q-181306.problem: Which of the following is a representation of the set $S=[-1,1]\times \{-1,1\}$ in the Cartesian plane?
q-181306.worked_solution:
The Cartesian product $A\times B$ consists of all ordered pairs whose first coordinate belongs to $A$ and whose second coordinate belongs to $B.$

$$
A\times B=\{(a,b)\,:\,a\in A,\,b\in B\}
$$

In this case, the set 

$$
S=[-1,1]\times \{-1,1\}
$$

contains every point in ${R}^{2}$ whose $x$-coordinate is any real number in the interval $[-1,1]$ and whose $y$-coordinate is either $-1$ or $1.$

$$
S=\{(x,y)\,:\,x\in [-1,1],\,y\in \{-1,1\}\}.
$$

To visualize $S$, consider ${S}_{1}⊂S$ containing all points whose $x$-coordinate is any real number in the interval $[-1,1]$ and whose $y$-coordinate equals $-1$

$$
{S}_{1}=\{(x,-1)\,:\,x\in [-1,1]\}
$$

This set is represented by the line segment shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14167512/assets/3ed05ffc58aad1a6c75e7862c1175f497fb14870e6650cc6c4ce01c3df091d8b.png)

Next, consider ${S}_{2}⊂S$ containing all points whose $x$-coordinate is any real number in the interval $[-1,1]$ and whose $y$-coordinate equals $1$

$$
{S}_{2}=\{(x,1)\,:\,x\in [-1,1]\}.
$$

This set is represented by the line segment shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14167512/assets/0f57920b2532177b0d64ac3dc95feb6a476bb385112d736d702895862e7de2b2.png)

Our Cartesian product is the *union* of these subsets:

$$
S={S}_{1}\cup {S}_{2}
$$

Therefore, $S$ can be represented by the two line segments shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14167512/assets/075454dae9ed36967a70537cdf3a3f59931cdd81671ff4059658d2e0df438898.png)

q-181770.name: Question 3
q-181770.problem: Which of the following is a representation of the set $S=Z\times R$ in the Cartesian plane?
q-181770.worked_solution:
The Cartesian product $A\times B$ consists of all ordered pairs whose first coordinate belongs to $A$ and whose second coordinate belongs to $B.$

$$
A\times B=\{(a,b)\,:\,a\in A,\,b\in B\}
$$

In this case, the set 

$$
S=Z\times R
$$

 
contains every point in ${R}^{2}$ whose $x$-coordinate is an integer number and whose $y$-coordinate is any real number.

$$
S=\{(x,y)\,:\,x\in Z,\,y\in R\}
$$

To visualize $S,$ consider ${S}_{-1}⊂S$ containing all points whose $x$-coordinate equals $-1$ and whose $y$-coordinate is any real number.

$$
{S}_{-1}=\{(-1,y)\,:\,y\in R\}
$$

We can represent ${S}_{-1}$ in the plane as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14167512/assets/3fdfed680e3fb46adbe8a70aac86682aacb85d43e0675923f87658635fc89a1e.png)

Next, consider ${S}_{1}⊂S$ containing all points whose $x$-coordinate equals $1$ and whose $y$-coordinate is any real number.

$$
{S}_{1}=\{(1,y)\,:\,y\in R\}.
$$

We can represent ${S}_{1}$ in the plane as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14167512/assets/7fbda500ecca7e18c9db9939ad78d4dcc6bf488bc7fc4de1137e764ce21a0254.png)

We can create the subsets $…,{S}_{-3},{S}_{-2},{S}_{0},{S}_{2},{S}_{3},…$ similarly. Our Cartesian product consists of the *union* of these subsets:

$$
\begin{aligned}R\times N & =…{S}_{-2}\cup {S}_{-1}\cup {S}_{0}\cup {S}_{1}\cup {S}_{2}… \\  & ={⋃}_{i\in Z}{S}_{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can visualize $Z\times R$ as the set of vertical lines shown in the diagram below.

q-184507.name: Question 5
q-184507.problem: Let $I=[0,1]⊂R$ and ${X}_{i}=[0,2]\times [-i,0].$ Which of the following represents ${⋂}_{i\in I}{X}_{i}?$
q-184507.worked_solution:
Recall that the intersection of a family of indexed sets consists of those elements that belong to *all* the sets:

$$
{⋂}_{i\in I}{A}_{i}=\{x\,:\,x\in {A}_{k}\,\,\text{for all}\,\,k\in I\}
$$

Let's now write down one of our indexed sets. For example, if $i=0.5,$ we have 

$$
{X}_{0.5}=[0,2]\times [-0.5,0]=\{(a,b)\,:\,a\in [0,2],b\in [-0.5,0]\}.
$$

This represents a rectangle whose vertices are at $(0,0),$ $(2,0),$ $(2,-0.5),$ and $(0,-0.5)$ in the coordinate plane, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14167512/assets/5837864bfcc40e680cf62b43c0e3d145ba05b1f25e1ccae2f4788902d030d927.png)

In general,

$$
{X}_{i}=[0,2]\times [-i,0]=\{(a,b)\,:\,a\in [0,2],b\in [-i,0]\}
$$

is the rectangle whose vertices are at $(0,0),$ $(2,0),$ $(2,-i),$ and $(0,-i).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14167512/assets/f0c20436f03db4b0003d087827cefbd76506af423da3f0a3042082b5afeb4b58.png)

The intersection of all these rectangles is the line segment $[0,2]\times \{0\}:$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14167512/assets/236d10f31265b400036e1ddeafa122991bcae1ea878af8b300003fb11acfa85b.png)
